judges.5.p1.b1.text: On that day Deborah and Barak son of Abinoam sang this song:

judges.5.p1.b2.text: “When the princes take the lead in Israel, when the people volunteer, bless the LORD.

judges.5.p1.b3.text: Listen, O kings! Give ear, O princes! I will sing to the LORD …

judges.5.p1.b4.text: O LORD, when You went out from Seir, when You marched from the land of Edom, the earth trembled, the heavens poured out rain, and the clouds poured down water. The mountains quaked before the LORD, …

judges.5.p2.b5.text: In the days of Shamgar son of Anath, in the days of Jael, the highways were deserted and the travelers took the byways.

judges.5.p2.b6.text: Life in the villages ceased; it ended in Israel, until I, Deborah, arose, a mother in Israel.

judges.5.p2.b7.text: When they chose new gods, then war came to their gates. Not a shield or spear was found among forty thousand in Israel.

judges.5.p2.b8.text: You who ride white donkeys, who sit on saddle blankets, and you who travel the road, ponder the voices of the singers at the watering places. There they shall recount the righteous acts of the LORD, …

judges.5.p3.b9.text: Awake, awake, O Deborah! Awake, awake, sing a song! Arise, O Barak, …

judges.5.p3.b10.text: Some came from Ephraim, with their roots in Amalek; Benjamin came with your people after you. … Issachar was with Barak, rushing into the valley at his heels.

judges.5.p3.b11.text: Why did you sit among the sheepfolds to hear the whistling for the flocks?

judges.5.p3.b12.text: Dan, why did you linger by the ships? Asher stayed at the coast and remained in his harbors.

judges.5.p3.b13.text: Zebulun was a people who risked their lives; Naphtali, too, on the heights of the battlefield.

judges.5.p4.b14.text: Kings came and fought; then the kings of Canaan fought at Taanach by the waters of Megiddo, but they took no plunder of silver.

judges.5.p4.b15.text: From the heavens the stars fought; from their courses they fought against Sisera.

judges.5.p4.b16.text: The River Kishon swept them away, the ancient river, the River Kishon.

judges.5.p4.b17.text: March on, O my soul, in strength!

judges.5.p4.b18.text: Then the hooves of horses thundered— the mad galloping of his stallions.

judges.5.p5.b19.text: Curse Meroz, … Bitterly curse her inhabitants; for they did not come to help the LORD, …

judges.5.p5.b20.text: Most blessed among women is Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite, …

judges.5.p5.b21.text: He asked for water, and she gave him milk. In a magnificent bowl she brought him curds.

judges.5.p5.b22.text: She reached for the tent peg, her right hand for the workman’s hammer. …

judges.5.p5.b23.text: At her feet he collapsed, he fell, … where he collapsed, there he fell dead.

judges.5.p6.b24.text: Sisera’s mother looked through the window; she peered through the lattice and lamented:

judges.5.p6.b25.text: Why is his chariot so long in coming? What has delayed the clatter of his chariots?

judges.5.p6.b26.text: Her wisest ladies answer; indeed she keeps telling herself,

judges.5.p6.b27.text: Are they not finding and dividing the spoil— … a plunder of dyed garments for Sisera, the spoil of embroidered garments …

judges.5.p7.b28.text: So may all your enemies perish, O LORD! But may those who love You shine like the sun at its brightest.

judges.5.p7.b29.text: And the land had rest for forty years.
